cards.text: The prophet Jeremiah has just asked the LORD why the wicked prosper (Jeremiah 12:1), and the LORD has answered him (Jeremiah 12:5-6). Now the LORD keeps speaking, and His words get heavy: "I have forsaken My house; I have abandoned My inheritance."

cards.question: The LORD calls His inheritance the beloved of His soul. He says He has given her into the hands of her ___.

cards.text: Then the LORD says what His inheritance has become to Him. She's like a lion in the forest, and friend, that is NOT the picture you stick on the fridge.

cards.question: The LORD says His inheritance has become like a lion in the forest. What has she done?

cards.text: And the LORD says, "therefore I hate her." Then the picture changes: she's like a speckled bird of prey.

cards.question: In the LORD's picture, the other birds of prey are circling to protect the speckled bird.
Then the LORD gives a command to gather something to devour His inheritance. What is to be gathered?

answers.text: All the beasts of the field
All the kings of the earth
All the armies of the north

cards.text: Lion, bird, and now a vineyard: three pictures in three verses, and I'm still tying my apron. The LORD calls it My vineyard, My plot of ground.

cards.question: Something has destroyed the LORD's vineyard and trampled His plot of ground. What was it?

cards.text: They turned His pleasant field into a desolate wasteland, and desolate before Him, the land mourns. Friend, when the GROUND is grieving, you know it's serious.

cards.question: All the land is laid waste, and the people take it deeply to heart.

cards.text: Over all the barren heights in the wilderness, the destroyers have come. No flesh has peace, friend, not one single person gets to exhale.

cards.question: The destroyers have come, for the sword of the ___ devours from one end of the earth to the other.

cards.text: They sowed wheat and harvested thorns. That's me back when my edges went soft: stamp a whole batch with love, pull out a tray of BLURRY BLOBS.

cards.question: After sowing wheat and harvesting thorns, the people have worn themselves out with nothing to show for it.
The LORD tells them to bear the shame of their harvest. Why?

cards.text: Then a new word comes: "This is what the LORD says". Now He talks about His evil neighbors, the ones who attack the inheritance He bequeathed to His people Israel.

cards.question: What is the LORD about to do to the evil neighbors who attack His people's inheritance?
The LORD says He will also uproot the house of Judah from among those neighbors.

cards.text: Two uprootings in one verse, and trust me, I know what getting moved out of your spot feels like: counter on Monday, junk drawer on Tuesday. Then the LORD says what comes after the uprooting.

cards.question: The LORD says He will never again show compassion to the ones He uproots.
After the uprooting, the LORD says He will bring each one back to his inheritance and to his own ___.

cards.text: Then comes an if: if they diligently learn the ways of His people and swear by His name, saying, "As surely as the LORD lives". DILIGENTLY, friend. That's not glancing at the group chat, that's reading every single message.

cards.question: The LORD says these neighbors once taught His people to swear by another name. Which one?
If the neighbors learn the ways of God's people and swear by the LORD's name, what happens to them?

answers.text: They will be established among His people
They will be made rulers over His people
They will be kept as His people's servants

cards.text: Then the LORD gives the other side of that if. This is the last word of His message, so lean in.

cards.question: But if they will not ___, the LORD says He will uproot that nation and destroy it.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the 'if' line ending with the quote, 'DILIGENTLY, friend.', and the group chat line. Only the opening card may run past two sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The question opens with 'But if they will not ___' and never says who 'they' are. It relies on the story card before it, which is no longer on screen. It should name the evil neighbors, or the nations the LORD uprooted.

rule.text: Always give context in the question. The story card before it isn't on screen anymore, so the question says who and what. Never "him," "that" or "it" pointing back to a card the baker can't see.

findings.problem: The question says 'The LORD tells them to bear the shame of their harvest' without saying who 'them' are. It points back to earlier cards for the people who sowed wheat and harvested thorns.
